chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Saʿid and Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi and al-ʿAbbas ibn Maʿruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abā al-Hasan Mūsā عليه السلام about a woman who experienced postnatal bleeding and remained so for thirty nights or more, then became pure and performed salat, then afterward saw blood or yellowish discharge. He said: “If it is yellowish discharge, then let her perform ghusl and perform salat, and she should not refrain from salat. But if it is blood that is not yellowish, then let her refrain from salat for the days of her menstrual period, then let her perform ghusl and perform salat.”

key_terms.أَيَّامَ قُرْئِهَا: the days of her menstrual cycle
key_terms.طَهُرَتْ: she became ritually pure from bleeding

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman sees blood or yellow discharge after becoming pure from nifas?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a woman who becomes pure after nifas and then later sees either yellowish discharge or blood. It distinguishes between the two: yellowish discharge does not stop salat after ghusl, while actual blood is treated according to the days of her menstrual cycle before she performs ghusl and resumes salat.
